title: IT / Finance / Security Admin Sync
summary: Weekly cross-functional sync to confirm April maintenance window, KMS rotation plan, SOC 2 artifact collection progress, and a proposed change to invoice approval flow. Owners and next steps assigned; plan to run a dry-run of maintenance in two weeks.
action_items: Marcus Powell: Draft maintenance runbook + rollback steps and share link to doc (due: 2026-04-17)
Omar Reyes: Prepare KMS rotation checklist and list of service accounts needing key access update (due: 2026-04-16)
Priya Nair: Update invoice approval flow diagram and sample emails for approvers (due: 2026-04-14)
Dina Alvarez: Upload missing SOC 2 evidence (access reviews, user offboarding logs) to the evidence bucket (due: 2026-04-20)
Evan Liu: Validate audit log retention policy in S3 and provide retention docs (due: 2026-04-18)
next_steps: Share updated SOC 2 evidence spreadsheet with auditors and CISO
Priya to circulate new invoice approval mockups and get sign-off from Finance leadership
transcript:
Header: 2026-04-10 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Jamie Park, Priya Nair, Omar Reyes, Evan Liu, Lara Chen, Marcus Powell, Dina Alvarez, Sofia Martins

[00:00] Jamie: Okay, good afternoon everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call - I see Lara, Marcus, Dina, Sofia, and then from platform we have Evan, from security Omar, and Priya from finance.
[00:12] Lara: Hi all, yep here.
[00:15] Marcus: Marcus here.
[00:18] Dina: Dina present.
[00:20] Sofia: Hi, Sofia.
[00:22] Evan: Evan on.
[00:24] Jamie: Cool. Agenda - maintenance window confirmation, KMS rotation, SOC 2 evidence check, invoice flow change, SSO cert renewal, audit logs. Anything to add?
[00:34] Priya: One quick finance note, we have a vendor invoice that needs a slightly different approval path - small change but need ops to confirm cutover.
[00:41] Jamie: Great, we'll cover it under invoice flow. Marcus, can you run through the maintenance window?
[00:47] Marcus: Yeah, so we are targeting the weekend of April 30th, 02:00-06:00 UTC, that's when traffic is lowest per the last month. Proposed scope: kernel updates on two prod clusters, redis restart for cache compaction, and a rolling update of the web fleet. We'll do canaries, and have rollback ready.
[01:06] Marcus: There's also the DB minor upgrade but we want to avoid long locks - so that one we probably push to next quarter unless necessary.
[01:12] Jamie: Ok, timeline looks fine. Any blockers? Omar?
[01:16] Omar: Security-wise the key concern is KMS rotation - some services use direct key access and we need to ensure automated provisioning can handle new KEKs. If rotation lands during the window, we need a tested path.
[01:28] Marcus: Right, that's why I'm suggesting we do KMS rotation as a pre-window task or a post-window task, not simultaneously.
[01:33] Dina: For SOC 2 evidence we actually need the access review artifacts showing that service accounts were rotated - auditors flagged a couple missing entries from Feb. If KMS rotation happens, can we ensure we record the change in the evidence bundle?
[01:46] Omar: Yes, I'll add the rotation action to the evidence tracker. I need Evan to confirm where the logs live and the retention headers.
[01:51] Evan: Logs are in the central S3 bucket under /audit/logs, retention policy set to 365 days by default, but for SOC 2 artifacts we keep exports in the evidence bucket for three years. I'll double-check lifecycle and document the exact key prefixes. Link to current retention doc: https://docs.redwood.internal/audit/retention (note: internal link).
[02:10] Lara: Good, auditors asked specifically for timestamped rotation events and the list of principals that changed access.
[02:15] Omar: I'll produce a CSV with service account names and the key IDs post-rotation.
[02:19] Jamie: OK action there. On KMS rotation approach - do we do a blind rotation or staged? Marcus?
[02:25] Marcus: Staged. We'll rotate keys for non-critical services first, run smoke tests, then the critical ones. The tricky bit is third-party services that store keys in their own vaults - we need to co-ordinate.
[02:36] Priya: On the finance side, related to vendor invoice - we want the approval to skip the manager queue for low-dollar vendor payments and go straight to finance for categorization then to accounting. That requires an update in the SAP/PLA workflow and an email template change.
[02:51] Sofia: For payroll-adjacent invoices, we need approval routing to include payroll lead.
[02:56] Priya: Yes we'll mark payroll ones as separate. I'll send mockups.
[03:00] Jamie: Cool. Any compliance concerns with changing approval flow? Dina?
[03:03] Dina: As long as we preserve segregation of duties and maintain audit trails (who approved and timestamps), it's fine. We need the approval metadata captured in the AP system and exported to the evidence store.
[03:13] Priya: We can add a required comment field and ID capture so accounting can reconcile.
[03:18] Marcus: Back to maintenance - can we clarify rollback triggers? CPU/memory anomalies for more than 2 minutes or error rate spikes over 2% on the canary clusters.
[03:29] Omar: Also if any service fails key rotation tests.
[03:32] Marcus: Agreed. I'll put metrics and thresholds into the runbook.
[03:36] Jamie: Good. Next - SAML/SSO cert renewal. Evan?
[03:40] Evan: Certificate for SAML metadata expires May 12th. We need to rotate certs in Okta and update SP metadata. There's a window of a few minutes where some logins might fail if metadata isn't updated on both sides. Proposed plan: prepare updated metadata, schedule a low-traffic update, and roll back if errors >1% login failures.
[03:58] Lara: Will users be able to fallback to password? We have some teams using passwordless.
[04:03] Dina: Okta supports fallback but it's messy. We should notify impacted teams.
[04:07] Priya: Send calendar notice ahead of rollout.
[04:09] Jamie: Action: Evan to prepare updated metadata and test in staging, Marcus to include SSO test in canaries.
[04:18] Evan: Will do, I'll post the staging test results to the runbook doc.
[04:22] [04:22] (crosstalk)
[04:24] Jamie: SOC 2 evidence status - Dina, what remains?
[04:27] Dina: Missing items: Feb access review exports, a few user offboarding logs, and evidence of account configuration change approvals. I've uploaded most but two items pending from IT and HR. I'll flag them in the tracker.
[04:38] Marcus: I have the offboarding logs - seems like two accounts had incomplete closure steps; will fill those entries by EOD Monday.
[04:44] Dina: Great, that helps. Also need proof of quarterly SSO configuration review - Evan, can you export the review notes?
[04:52] Evan: Yep, will pull the Confluence page and export PDF to evidence bucket.
[04:56] Jamie: Good. A quick note on audit logs and retention - we discussed extending retention for some services to 2 years for legal hold. Evan?
[05:05] Evan: It's feasible but will increase storage costs. I estimate a 15% incremental cost for the audit bucket. We can do lifecycle transition to infrequent access after 90 days to reduce cost.
[05:16] Lara: Finance needs the number - can you send a small cost estimate?
[05:19] Evan: Yes I'll send a one-pager.
[05:22] Priya: Back to invoices - we have a merchant that changed tax ID and the invoice was flagged. We need to confirm vendor validation step gets updated before auto-approval.
[05:33] Marcus: Are we automating vendor validation?
[05:35] Priya: Partially, but for changes we manual-review. I'm proposing a hold rule: if vendor tax ID changes, route to finance for verification.
[05:43] Sofia: I'll support that since payroll-adjacent vendors can affect taxes.
[05:46] Jamie: Okay, next - who owns comms to internal teams for the maintenance? Marcus?
[05:49] Marcus: I'll own the comms; will send a draft email and a changelog. Need PR team to post a banner.
[05:55] Lara: Please include a note for integrations owners - e.g., partners on the API side.
[05:59] Marcus: Will do.
[06:02] Jamie: Any blockers on the KMS rotation checklist? Omar?
[06:05] Omar: I need the list of services that use the old key. Evan, can you export that mapping?
[06:09] Evan: Yes, I have it in the secrets mapping. I'll export to CSV and mark the owners.
[06:13] Omar: Also want to confirm CI/CD pipelines won't break - some pipelines pull keys at build time. We'll need to update pipeline variables.
[06:21] Evan: Noted, I'll add pipeline owners to the runbook and sequence variable updates.
[06:27] Jamie: Alright, let's recap actions before we close. Marcus?
[06:31] Marcus: I'll draft maintenance runbook, define rollback thresholds, and send comms (due: 2026-04-17).
[06:37] Omar: I'll prepare KMS rotation checklist and CSV of service accounts (due: 2026-04-16).
[06:40] Priya: I'll update invoice flow and send mockups (due: 2026-04-14).
[06:44] Dina: I'll finish SOC 2 missing artifacts upload (due: 2026-04-20).
[06:47] Evan: I'll validate log retention and export SAML review notes (due: 2026-04-18).
[06:51] Lara: Finance will review cost estimate when Evan sends it.
[06:54] Jamie: Great, we'll schedule a dry-run for the maintenance for April 24th; calendar invite to follow. Any other items?
[06:59] Sofia: Quick question - for the vendor invoice routing change, do we need legal sign-off?
[07:03] Priya: Not for the flow change itself, only for contract changes.
[07:06] Jamie: OK. Thanks everyone. We'll share the updated runbook and SOC 2 tracker after the call.
[07:12] (meeting ends)

Notes: Some transcript auto-captions messed up minor proper nouns; speakers confirmed via roll call. Shared artifacts referenced: runbook draft (link to internal doc), SOC2 evidence tracker (spreadsheet link), invoice flow mockups (to be shared by Priya).
